reasons: Two clear tests cover the flagged case and the allowed case.
The test checks the legal reference text, so message changes will show up.

terms.meaning: a small program that checks another part of the code behaves as expected

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for ownership tests
sections.what: Brings in the path type and the ownership check code under test.
sections.why: Needed so the tests can run the check. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: test_forbidden_transfer_function_fires
sections.title: Forbidden transfer test
sections.what: Checks that a function named for transferring ownership is flagged once with the right code and legal reference.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the main rule still fires. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the legal reference text changes, this test fails on purpose.

sections.name: test_evidence_recording_does_not_fire
sections.title: Evidence recording test
sections.what: Checks that a function that records an externally registered instrument is not flagged.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the allowed approach is not blocked by the rule. Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Tests that the ownership check flags a transfer function and does not flag a function that only records evidence.
purpose: Proves the ownership rule catches the forbidden case and leaves the allowed case alone.
why: Likely reason: checks both sides of the rule so it neither misses nor over-flags. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Gives the checker a function named transfer ownership and expects one violation with the right code and legal reference. Then gives it a function that records an instrument and expects no violations.
inputs: Two small pieces of Python source written inside the tests.
outputs: Pass or fail results for the two checks.
risks: Only two cases are covered, so many other name patterns are not tested.
debug: If a test fails, compare the code it passes in with the rule patterns in the ownership check.
